body.name: Profile-slice composite-test inversion handle
body.construction: For a reference \(h\in H_m\), endpoint index \(v\), connected target slice \(B_0\subseteq[0,a_m]\), and degree \(D\ge n\), begin with \[\min_{0\le u_{\omega}\le1}\sum_{\omega\in\Omega_{n,m}}f_h(\omega)u_{\omega}\quad\text{subject to}\quad\sum_{\omega\in\Omega_{n,m}}f_g(\omega)u_{\omega}\ge1-\delta_0/4\quad\forall g\in H_m\text{ with }T_v(g)\in B_0.\] On each of the \(2^{2m}\) sign orthants, write \(g\) as the signed version of \(\zeta\in[0,a_m]^{2m}\), triangulate the cube intersected with the two linear slice inequalities, elevate the degree \(n\) count-likelihood polynomial to Bernstein degree \(D\), and impose nonnegativity of every Bernstein coefficient of \(\sum_{\omega}f_g(\omega)u_{\omega}-(1-\delta_0/4)\) on every simplex. This is a conservative linear program with \(\binom{n+32m-1}{32m-1}\) acceptance variables and at most \(2^{2m}\binom{\binom{4m+2}{2m}}{2m+1}\binom{D+2m}{2m}\) coefficient inequalities per target slice, using the vertex bound for a \(2m\)-polytope with \(4m+2\) facet inequalities. Invert nested accepted slices and coordinate the two endpoint tests within the joint level budget. The resulting degree-indexed family is \(\mathfrak H_{n,m}\); the open task includes proving an explicit sufficient degree or a sharper orbit-reduced complexity bound.
